2.name: text_block

0.name: block
0.value:
mag_yaw_correct turns individual joints of a 20-joint pose about the vertical, to take out heading errors that a magnetometer has put into the suit data.

THE SLIDERS:
Every joint has two sliders, in degrees:
  head, neck, spine3 ... r_wrist             the global correction
  head_cal, neck_cal ... r_wrist_cal         the local correction

They follow the 20 active joints in order: head is the base of the skull, neck the upper vertebrae, spine3, spine2 and spine1 the mid vertebrae, lower vertebrae and spine pelvis, pelvis the pelvis anchor, then hips, knees and ankles, and l_collar / r_collar the shoulder blades, then shoulders, elbows and wrists.

TWO CORRECTIONS, AND THEY ARE DIFFERENT:
The global correction turns the joint about the vertical of the room. A value of 10 turns it by -10 degrees: you enter the error, and it is taken back out. It is meant for an ongoing magnetometer error - the sensor's heading being wrong in the room.

The local correction turns the joint about its own up axis (its y axis, which is vertical in the T-pose), by the value as given. It is meant for an error baked in at calibration - the sensor's idea of its T-pose being turned on the limb.

A global error comes from the field around the sensor, so a fixed global correction may hold in one part of the room and not another; a local one is fixed to the limb and holds everywhere.

EACH JOINT ON ITS OWN:
The corrections act on each joint's orientation in the room, and the pose is then turned back into joint-to-joint rotations. So correcting one joint does not carry the joints below it: in the example the elbows are turned and the wrists keep the direction they had, which shows up as the opposite turn in the wrist rows. Each sensor's error is its own, so this is what you want.

symmetric AND sync:
Both are on by default and act when you move a slider. 'symmetric' copies the value to the same slider on the other side - hip, knee, ankle, collar, shoulder, elbow, wrist - with the same sign. 'sync local/global' copies a joint's global value to its local slider and back, so the joint gets both turns with the same angle. That is right when the magnetic error is the same at every orientation of the sensor. Note that for a joint that is upright and only turned about the vertical, the two then cancel, and you will see no change.

WHAT IT TAKES:
A 20-joint pose, 20 rows of w x y z (or the same 80 numbers in one row), from active_joints, active_pose or a take. A 37-row pose straight from shadow is ignored - put active_joints in between. With every slider at zero the pose passes through unchanged.

SYNTAX:
mag_yaw_correct

EXAMPLE:
mag_yaw_correct

INPUTS and PARAMETERS:

pose in:
The 20-joint pose to correct.

symmetric:
Copy each slider move to the other side. On by default.

sync local/global:
Tie each joint's global and local sliders together. On by default.

reset:
Set every slider back to zero.

head ... r_wrist:
The global corrections, in degrees.

head_cal ... r_wrist_cal:
The local corrections, in degrees.

OUTPUT:

pose out:
The corrected 20-joint pose.

RELATED:
mag_offset measures a sensor's magnetic offset.
shadow_arm_correct fits and corrects a fixed upper-arm error. pose_adjust applies fixed corrections joint by joint.
